question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,\,2z,\,y-2⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=2x-y+1$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

*Hint: You're given that the fundamental vector product of $S$ with respect to its canonical parametrization is $||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||=\sqrt{6}.$*
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

Notice that our surface $z=2x-y+1$ can be written using the dot product as 

$$
⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨-2,\,1,\,1⟩}_{⏟}}_{-\overset{~}{n}}=1,\,\text{or}\,⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩\cdot {{⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{\overset{~}{n}}=-1.
$$

Since we require a downward-pointing normal vector to our surface $S,$ we must select one where the $z$-component is negative. This gives us the normal vector

$$
\overset{~}{n}=⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩.
$$

Normalizing this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{\overset{~}{n}}{‖\overset{~}{n}‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $z=2x-y+1$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨3x,\,2z,\,y-2⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟨3x,\,4x-2y+2,\,y-2⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(6x-(4x-2y+2)-(y-2)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+y).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+y)\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+y)\cdot ||{r}_{x}\times {r}_{y}||\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}(2x+y)\cdot \sqrt{6}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{1}{\cancel{\sqrt{6}}}(2x+y)\cdot \cancel{\sqrt{6}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4}(2x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}+xy]}_{x=0}^{x=4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4y+16)\,\text{d}y \\  & =[2{y}^{2}+16y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$
